basics.name: Angello Portillo
basics.label: Project Engineering Intern
basics.summary: Project engineering intern delivering secure, cloud-connected systems for Hawai‘i’s Med-QUEST program while modernizing public-sector IT. I blend full-stack development, Azure/AWS infrastructure, and hands-on field support to keep critical services resilient, data-driven, and compliant.

work.summary: Enhancing the Med-QUEST member services platform by redesigning workflows, integrating secure APIs, and deploying database architectures across Microsoft Entra, Azure, and Oracle services to boost scalability and compliance.

work.company: State of Hawai'i Department of Labor & Industrial Relations
work.summary: Provided on-site technical support for government-issued hardware, software, and secure networks while maintaining AWS environments that power statewide services.

As Team Lead for the Hawaii Space Grant Consortium, I guided a team of interns in designing and launching a NASA-sponsored high-powered rocket aimed at achieving specific flight goals such as target apogee and successful recovery. I was responsible for developing the avionics bay, where I programmed microcontrollers to interface with sensors that measured altitude and controlled the timed deployment of drogue and main parachutes. I also integrated a GPS tracking system to ensure safe and accurate post-flight recovery, while coordinating team efforts and maintaining compliance with NASA’s technical and safety standards throughout the project.

At the ARLISS event with AeroPac, I built and launched my own high-powered rocket, using simulation software to predict its flight path and ensure a safe recovery. It was an incredible hands-on experience—designing, testing, and refining my rocket alongside fellow enthusiasts. I also earned my Level 1 High Power Rocketry Certification from Tripoli.

work.company: NASA - National Aeronautics and Space Administration
work.summary: At the ROCK ON NASA Workshop at Wallops, we designed and built custom PCB boards equipped with sensors and an Arduino, programmed to collect flight data. After integrating our payload into a high-powered sounding rocket, we launched it into the upper atmosphere and analyzed the recovered flight data.

Provided consistent, high-quality customer service at a licensed Starbucks inside Target during the COVID-19 pandemic. Developed teamwork, communication, multitasking, and time management skills while adapting to evolving safety protocols and high-pressure environments.
